title: One outsider can fill the daily help limit for every gym, and the AI import limit too
what: Help and feedback lets each network address send 20 messages a day, but all gyms and members together share one ceiling of 1,000 a day. Someone using about 50 addresses (easy on mobile data) can use up the whole day's allowance, and then every owner, desk and member who writes for help that day is told 'Too many messages today'. The AI that matches columns in a member import works the same way: 20 a day per gym but 1,000 a day for all gyms together, and free trial gyms cost nothing to make, so a few dozen made-up gyms switch AI import matching off for everyone for the day.
expected: One person or a handful of addresses cannot stop real gyms from writing for help or using AI import. The shared ceiling only counts signed-in gyms, or each gym keeps its own share that strangers cannot use.
how_often: only if someone sets out to do it
fix_line: Keep help messages from signed-in gyms and members outside the shared ceiling, and count the AI import ceiling only for paying or checked gyms

title: A help question sent without a sign-in key still gets a free AI answer that no gym pays for
what: Help answers are meant to come out of the gym's AI credits (20 questions for one credit). But when a question arrives with no member key and no admin sign-in key, the server skips the credit check and still asks the AI. Anyone who calls the help address directly, or uses an app with the key taken out, gets AI answers for free, up to 20 a day per address; a gym with no credits left can do the same to get around the 'no credit' help-pages answer. MettleUp pays for these from its own monthly AI budget.
expected: A question with no key gets the help-pages answer, or is counted against a small free allowance, never a free AI answer.
how_often: every time someone sends a question without a key
fix_line: Answer a question with no key from the help pages only
